label: copied input l early in copy phase (recall_idx 1-2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is the letter l, almost exclusively at the first two copy-input steps (recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the input is original token 0 or 1 = l). Strongest when l is the first original token and is input right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, top activations ~3.9); weaker at recall_idx 2, and only faint residual activity at recall_idx 3+ (about 2.5% of mass). Magnitude also grows with how many outputs remain (longer sequences); in short sequences (L<=5) with few outputs left it often does not fire, which accounts for most false positives. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and never on any token other than l (one stray digit 2 activation).

issues: All factual claims check out on the dev profile. It never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter (0 activations each). In the copy phase in_tok=l accounts for 100% of mass, with only 1 stray activation on the digit 2. By recall_idx, mass share is 0.541 at 1, 0.433 at 2, 0.025 at 3 and about 0 at 4 and later. Activation rate rises with to_go: 0.001 at to_go=1, 0.011 at to_go=6.
Test score reproduced: P 0.880, R 0.921, F1 0.900, mass recall 0.975.

Missed activations (2.5% of mass) are almost all weak (0.01-0.24 of max) firings on l at recall_idx 3. Adding recall_idx==3 hurts: it has precision 0.15 alone, and recall_idx<=3 with to_go>=3 gives F1 0.80. Even OR-ing (recall_idx==3 & to_go>=5) into the to_go>=2 rule gives F1 0.888. So these misses are the weak tail the explanation already describes, not a class to add.

False positives are l at recall_idx 1 or 2 in short sequences with few outputs left, as the explanation says. to_go>=2 gives test P 0.936, R 0.881, F1 0.908, a marginal gain that matches the reported 0.91. A repeated 'l l' prefix is not a systematic false-positive class: recall_idx==2 with previous input l still fires at precision 0.99.
Minor point: the label is phrased as 'early in copy phase', but the real dependence is on recall_idx, which is what the predicate encodes. The label does not overclaim.
